Chapter 6: The Power of Service and Contribution
Have you ever noticed how things shift when you stop asking, "What do I want from life?" and start wondering, "What can I give?" That simple change in perspective—it can quietly mark a turning point on your path to finding purpose.
For so many of us, real meaning often nudges us outward, away from our own wants and toward the needs of others. It’s about discovering how your gifts—big or small—can truly make a difference.
Let me share a story. There was a retired engineer who felt a little lost after leaving his job. Looking for something to fill his days, he began volunteering at a local library. At first, it seemed pretty routine. But as he started helping kids with their homework, something sparked inside him—a kind of joy he hadn’t felt in years. The look of gratitude in those children’s eyes, celebrating even tiny victories together... it brought him a sense of fulfillment no paycheck ever could.
We often underestimate the impact of small acts of service, don’t we? It’s easy to think only grand gestures matter. But the truth is, purpose often shows up in the ordinary moments. Think about a neighbor who checks in on an elderly friend, a teenager tutoring someone who’s struggling, or a parent volunteering at a food bank. These are the quiet threads weaving meaning into everyday life.
Over time, a lot of people discover that contribution isn’t about losing yourself in others’ needs or giving up what you want. It’s about recognizing those unique ways you can add value to the world. Take, for example, a woman who loved to bake. She started bringing treats to her coworkers just for fun. That simple gesture grew into a weekly ritual—lifting moods, building community, and inspiring more kindness than she ever imagined.
Here’s something to pay attention to: service has a way of putting your own struggles into perspective. One man, going through a tough divorce, found comfort by mentoring young people at a community center. Listening to their stories, he realized everyone faces challenges. And by being there for them, he found healing and a sense of connection he truly needed.
Now, maybe the idea of service feels overwhelming sometimes—like you have to give up your dreams to help others. But most people realize, true contribution isn’t about sacrificing yourself. It’s about finding that sweet spot where your joy and the world’s needs overlap. When you share your gifts—whether it’s a skill, a talent, or simply a listening ear—you create meaning for yourself and for those around you.
So, what’s the key takeaway? The path to purpose isn’t a lonely road. It’s shaped by relationships, by the ways we show up for each other, and by our willingness to give what we can. In serving others, many of us discover we’re also serving ourselves—uncovering strengths and possibilities we never knew we had.
